subject: Clearline MAP: performance execution & gap analysis
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance scoping (next steps)

Priya — thanks again for the MAP kickoff yesterday. Per our call I pulled together an execution plan for the performance benchmarking portion (latency/throughput/TTFT + concurrency). High level: we will run two phases (dev verification, then production-like stress) and deliver a short gap analysis with recommended mitigations.

Key asks from your side: sample production prompts (or representative prompt profiles), a target SLO table, and a 1-week window where we can run sustained load against a mirrored workspace.

Proposed scoping (short):
- Workload slices: 30% short (<=32 tokens), 50% medium (64–256 tokens), 20% long (>256 tokens)
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 64 concurrent clients
- TTFT measurement: time-to-first-byte and time-to-first-token on first generation request (cold vs warm KV cache)
- Throughput targets: baseline (shared capacity) and dedicated capacity (+burst)
- Acceptance criteria (initial draft): median TTFT < 120 ms; p95 TTFT < 300 ms; sustained throughput >= 800 tokens/sec for the medium slice at 32 concurrent clients

Attachments: I attached the load plan YAML (clearline_load_plan.yml) and a template results CSV. Please review and send your prompt samples and a preferred 2-day test window.

Next steps:
- Priya: share prompt samples and confirm 2-day window
- Marissa & Karthik: we’ll finalize the exact harness parameters and quantization knobs to test

Thanks — happy to sync if you want to walk through.

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance scoping (next steps)

Thanks Jonas — attaching a representative sample set (short, medium, long) and a link to our anonymized traffic profile. We can give you the window Aug 18–19 for the production-like run; engineering will stand by.

Couple clarifications:
- The long slice is pretty heavy on context (we often include patient history blobs). For these requests, p95 latency for the *full response* is what our UX team watches — but for the MAP we understand TTFT and first-token are critical for perceived latency.
- Throughput expectation: our ops team prefers guaranteed 1k tokens/sec sustained for medium slice during business hours. If that’s unrealistic on shared capacity we’re prepared to evaluate Dedicated.

Attachments included: sample_prompts.json, traffic_profile.csv

Priya Shah
VP, Product — Clearline Health
priya.shah@clearlinehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance scoping (next steps)

Thanks Priya — received the samples and traffic profile. We validated tokenization and produced an initial mapping of your profile into three workload slices (attached). A couple of concrete updates to scope based on the samples:

- Revised workload mix (by request count): short 25%, medium 55%, long 20% (your medium messages skew slightly longer than we estimated)
- SLOs (proposal):
  * TTFT first-token (warm cache): median <= 100 ms; p95 <= 250 ms
  * TTFT cold-first-request: median <= 300 ms; p95 <= 600 ms
  * End-to-end full-response latency (long slice) p95 <= 2.5s (informational — not blocking for MAP pass)
  * Sustained throughput (medium slice) >= 1,000 tokens/sec at 32 concurrent clients on Dedicated capacity; >= 700 tokens/sec on Shared baseline
- Success criteria: pass if all warm-cache TTFT SLOs met and sustained throughput within 10% of Dedicated target (we’ll flag gaps and remediation).

We’ll run the dev verification on Aug 17 (low load) and the production-like stress on Aug 18–19. I’m cc’ing Karthik to capture that we will test the quantized LLM variant and the non-quantized baseline.

Attachments: mapped_workload_slices.csv, updated_slos_table.xlsx

—
Marissa Cole
Performance PM, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearlinehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: MAP execution — preliminary observations (Aug 18–19 run)

Priya / team — quick summary of what we observed during the Aug 18–19 production-like run:

What we executed:
- Workload: mapped slices from Marissa’s file (short/medium/long), request mix reproduced from traffic_profile.csv
- Variants tested: baseline (FP16) on shared capacity; quantized INT8 variant on Dedicated; two routing policies (latency-first, cost-first)
- Concurrency sweep: 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 clients

Preliminary numbers (medium slice, warm cache, 32 clients):
- Baseline (shared): median TTFT 140 ms, p95 TTFT 410 ms, sustained throughput 720 tokens/sec
- Dedicated (INT8): median TTFT  ninety-eight ms, p95 TTFT 280 ms, sustained throughput 1,080 tokens/sec

Notable gaps: p95 on shared baseline exceeded the proposed p95 SLO (250 ms). Dedicated + INT8 met the majority of warm-cache SLOs but p95 is close to the edge for some long-backed requests (context-heavy).

Initial action items we recommend:
1) Route high-context long requests to Dedicated capacity or a cold-optimized variant.
2) Enable prefix KV caching for repeated patient-history chunks — we measured ~20–30% p95 improvement when the cache hit rate increased.
3) Consider INT8 quantization in production for medium/short slices to reduce p95 and increase throughput; we will validate quality regression on your eval set but initial checks are promising.

I uploaded the raw CSV (clearline_map_bench_results.csv) and a short gap analysis (redwood_map_gap_analysis.pdf) to the Drive link. We’ll follow up with a short write-up that pairs each gap with remediation cost and estimated lead time.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP execution — preliminary observations (Aug 18–19 run)

Thanks Karthik — the team reviewed the CSV and the gap analysis. A few notes from Clearline:

- We’re pleased Dedicated + INT8 hits the throughput target and improves median TTFT. The p95 on some long requests is still a concern for clinician UX; routing makes sense as a pragmatic short-term fix.
- We want to see the quality regression verification before enabling INT8 globally — please share the eval set results when ready.
- Next steps agreed:
  1) Redwood to produce the remediation-cost matrix (impact, estimated engineering time, infra cost) by Aug 28.
  2) Clearline to review and decide on Dedicated procurement by Sep 8.
  3) Schedule a 30-minute decision call the week of Sep 1 — propose Sep 2 10:00 PT.

Please confirm delivery on Aug 28 for the remediation matrix and the eval-results for INT8. We’ll mark this MAP bench phase as "informational pass" until we close the remediation items.

Thanks —
Priya Shah
VP, Product — Clearline Health
priya.shah@clearlinehealth.com
